title: Nonlocality effects on fermions confined within a hard-wall potential
authors: G. Q. Garcia, P. J. Porfírio, E. Brito, D. C. Moreira
abstract: We investigate nonlocality effects on the energy spectrum of spin-$1/2$ fermions confined by hard-wall potentials. Starting from a nonlocal Dirac theory with a modified kinetic term, we formulate the associated field equation in flat spacetime using cylindrical coordinates. By exploiting the eigenvalue spectrum of the squared Dirac operator, the original infinite-order equation is reduced to a finite-order problem. We also show that on the branch continuously connected to the local Dirac theory the nonlocal corrections can be encoded in an effective fermion mass. We then find analytical energy spectra for two confining geometries: a cylindrical hard wall and a quantum ring defined by two concentric cylindrical boundaries. In both cases, the radial equations reduce to Bessel equations and the boundary conditions quantize the allowed modes. The local hard-wall spectra are recovered for $Λ\to\infty$, whereas finite nonlocality shifts the mass contribution and, consequently, the particle--antiparticle energy separation. These results provide a direct characterization of nonlocal effects in quantum-confined fermionic systems.
summary: This theoretical work analyzes the energy spectrum of confined fermions subjected to nonlocality effects modeled via a modified Dirac equation. The authors derive analytical solutions for cylindrical and quantum ring geometries, showing that nonlocality primarily shifts the effective mass term in the energy eigenvalues. This provides a quantitative characterization of how non-local physics modifies quantum confinement predictions.
main_problem: The paper investigates how nonlocality modifies the energy spectrum of spin-1/2 fermions confined within a hard-wall potential.
main_result: Nonlocal effects are shown to modify the mass contribution to the energy spectrum, leading to analytical spectra for cylindrical and quantum ring geometries, while recovering the local results in the limit of infinite nonlocality scale.
method: The authors derive a nonlocal Dirac equation, reduce it to a finite-order problem using the eigenvalue spectrum of the squared Dirac operator, and solve the resulting radial equations using Bessel functions.
model_or_system: The system consists of spin-1/2 fermions confined by hard-wall potentials in flat spacetime, analyzed in cylindrical coordinates for geometries like a cylindrical box or a quantum ring.
key_observables: The energy spectrum ($E_{n,j}$), particularly the shift in the particle--antiparticle energy separation.
important_parameters: The nonlocality parameter ($\Lambda$), the effective mass ($M_{	ext{eff}}$), and the confinement radii ($r_0, R_1, R_2$).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes a flat spacetime background and focuses on the branch of the theory continuously connected to the local Dirac theory.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the energy levels for fermions in a cylinder and a ring as a function of confinement size, demonstrating the dependence on quantum numbers and nonlocality.
paper_structure: The paper proceeds by formulating the nonlocal Dirac equation, simplifying it via the squared Dirac operator, determining the effective mass $M_{	ext{eff}}$, and finally solving the resulting radial equations for the specific geometries (cylinder and ring) using Bessel functions.
why_interesting: While focused on fermions, the methodology of solving confinement problems in low-dimensional geometries (rings/cylinders) and incorporating non-local corrections via effective mass terms is highly relevant to modeling exotic quantum systems in AMO physics.
